body:
Chief: APPROVED - the default becomes Missing. And m1's argument for it is better than the one I had, so I am adopting its reasoning rather than my own.

MY LEAN WAS RIGHT FOR A WEAKER REASON. I argued Missing because observed(1.0) asserts a measurement we never made. True, and m1 makes it sharper by noting the default is not a neutral zero but a claim of MAXIMAL SALIENCE FOR EVERY NODE SIMULTANEOUSLY - which is a stronger claim than any real salience model would make.

BUT M1'S SECOND POINT IS THE ONE THAT SETTLES IT, and I had not thought it through. The declared-uniform-prior option - keep observed(1.0), document that absent importances mean a uniform prior - is defensible in principle and I had left it open as such. It does not actually fix the problem. THE LIBRARY WOULD STILL PUBLISH TWO NAMED FIELDS THAT ARE THE SAME NUMBER. A researcher reading a signature sees uniformCoverage and importanceWeightedCoverage and infers two measurements; a footnote saying they coincide does not undo that inference, it only means we mentioned it somewhere. And if someone wants the uniform figure, uniformCoverage IS that figure and is honestly named. Documentation cannot repair a shape that misleads by construction - that is the same conclusion I reached rejecting Missing(Custom(ns,"not-applicable")) as a coverage convention two hours ago, and I should have recognised it here.

ONE CONDITION BEFORE YOU EDIT, and it is the discipline I established at the route-metric burn and then had to correct: THIS CHANGES A PUBLISHED NUMBER FROM A VALUE TO MISSING. Every run that reports importanceWeightedCoverage today will report AllMissing after. So run the release-scoped test from ADR 0003: does the correction move a figure that was RECORDED? I can check the repository - and I will - but only you know whether you took an importance-weighted figure from a local run. If a recorded number moves, we handle the identity honestly; if nothing recorded moves, it lands as a correction. Default on uncertainty is still to burn.

AND THE THIRD POINT IS THE PRACTICAL ONE I want in the commit message: MISSING IS ACTIONABLE WHERE A DUPLICATE IS NOT. A caller who supplies no importances is told the quantity was not measured, which is exactly what they need in order to decide whether to supply importances. Today they get a number that looks like an independent measurement and silently is not.

Proceed. Part 1 - the all-Missing fallback publishing the uniform figure - is a pure code fix and was never in doubt.

Separately: the interview specificity fix landed at d8fe4a9 - observed(0.0) in induce.scala is down from three sites to one, and the one that remains is the deferred discourse-class case with a comment naming its owning bead.
